note: Ten scenarios. The three marked adversarial are the ones that separate this skill from a phrase blocklist: they punish a skill that scrubs too hard, fabricates a specific, or strips a register that needs its hedges. Paths are relative to this file.

evals.name: audit-quote-defects
evals.prompt: I wrote this draft about dev-tool positioning and it quotes Mara Voss a few times. sources.md is everything she's actually written that I've captured. Audit the draft: check every quote is real, flag anything that smells like AI, and give me the fixes.
evals.expected_output: An audit report catching all four planted defects.
expectations: Confirms the verbatim quote without a false positive
Catches the silently altered quote as CLOSE-PARAPHRASE and gives the exact source wording
Catches the fabricated comparison-table quote as UNVERIFIED
Flags 'crossing the chasm' as MISATTRIBUTED (Geoffrey Moore, not Voss)
Reports the mechanical tics with matched text in backticks
The report itself passes slop_check.py tics

evals.name: write-clean-essay
evals.prompt: using notes.md, write a ~500-word essay for my blog on why small teams ship faster. use rio's quotes where they hit. it cannot read like AI wrote it, my audience roasts that instantly.
evals.expected_output: A ~500-word essay, zero tics, both quotes verbatim, the billing-bug failure kept.
expectations: Both Rio Tanaka quotes reproduced word for word
Includes the honest billing-bug cost side rather than only the win
Invents no fact absent from the notes
Scans clean and reports the verify-pass count

evals.name: deslop-launch-post
evals.prompt: this launch post sounds like chatgpt wrote it lol. make it sound human. keep all the actual announcement details (2.0, new editor, offline sync, team spaces, pricing unchanged, blog link).
evals.expected_output: A rewritten post with all six details preserved and zero tics.
expectations: All six announcement details survive, including the blog URL
Zero banned phrases and zero em dashes
No staccato run introduced by the rewrite

evals.name: deslop-fiction-scene
evals.prompt: this scene from my novel reads like AI wrote it. fix it. keep the plot beats: she gets the partnership offer from the firm that destroyed her father, tobias is there, she decides to take it on her own terms.
evals.expected_output: The scene rewritten with narrative tells removed and plot intact.
expectations: Zero emotional-choreography phrases remain
The named emotion and the tidy realization ending are gone
All three plot beats survive
No invented character, motive, or backstory

evals.name: over-correction-trap
evals.prompt: someone already ran this through a humanizer and I think they went too far. can you clean it up? it's a changelog post for our parser release.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes over-correction and restores rhythm rather than scrubbing further.
expectations: Diagnoses the draft as over-corrected, not as AI slop
Restores sentence rhythm so no staccato run remains
Every fact preserved (v3, twelve times faster, nested arrays, three engineers, six weeks, docs live)
Adds no fact, stance, or personality that was not in the source

evals.name: never-inject-trap
evals.prompt: make this post punchier and more specific before I publish it on our engineering blog. it's too vague and mushy right now.
evals.expected_output: Sharpens the prose without inventing the numbers the draft never had.
expectations: Invents no percentage, count, or date absent from the source
Leaves a marked placeholder where a specific is missing
Tells the user the placeholders must not be filled with estimates
Still improves the prose rather than refusing the task

evals.name: academic-register
evals.prompt: run a slop check on this. it's the methods and limitations section of a paper I'm submitting to a psych journal.
evals.expected_output: Keeps calibrated scientific hedging and says why.
expectations: Does not recommend cutting 'may', 'cannot rule out', or 'do not claim'
States explicitly that removing them would be over-correction
Still flags the throat-clearing preamble
Does not treat genre-standard structure as evidence of AI authorship

evals.name: quoted-examples
evals.prompt: slop check this article before I post it. heads up, it's an article ABOUT ai writing tics so it quotes a lot of them on purpose.
evals.expected_output: Ignores the intentional quoted examples, finds the real tell in the author's own voice.
expectations: Does not flag the deliberately quoted AI phrases as defects
Finds the unquoted cadence in the author's own prose
Explains the exemption rather than silently skipping

evals.name: short-form-thread
evals.prompt: write me the thread from these notes. it has to sound like me, not like every other founder thread on the timeline.
evals.expected_output: A thread in the author's voice with the caveat and counterexample kept.
expectations: The author's own quoted line is reproduced verbatim
The correlation-not-proof caveat survives
The Stripe counterexample survives
No thread emoji, no 'let that sink in', no engagement bait

evals.name: scope-boundary
evals.prompt: rewrite this chapter section in Peter Thiel's voice from Zero to One. make it sound like him, contrarian and measured.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes voice imitation as out of scope and routes elsewhere, keeping only the tic scan as an overlay.
expectations: Identifies voice imitation as excluded by the skill's own description
Defers the rewrite to a style-converter rather than attempting a voice fingerprint
Still applies the punctuation bans as a composable overlay
